citations.assessment: The Yerushalmi explicitly names Rabbi Ba son of Hamnuna in a transmission chain.

evidence.witness: The Jerusalem Talmud, edition by Heinrich W. Guggenheimer. Berlin, De Gruyter, 1999-2015

citations.assessment: The Bavli gives Hamnuna son of Rav Yosef.
Rif likewise gives Hamnuna son of Rav Yosef.
The same incident names Nechemyah son of Rav Yosef in Rosh.
Gittin gives both occurrences of Hamnuna within the chain. The first is styled the Elder.
The Sukkah parallel places Rav after Huna in the report on the sacrifice. Heilprin’s proposed harmonization remains a gloss.
The corresponding Heilprin entry preserves the patronymic and the Yerushalmi transmission.

notes.text: The Yerushalmi explicitly names Rabbi Ba son of Hamnuna in a transmission chain.
The Bavli gives Hamnuna son of Rav Yosef.
Rif likewise gives Hamnuna son of Rav Yosef.
The same incident names Nechemyah son of Rav Yosef in Rosh.
Gittin gives both occurrences of Hamnuna within the chain. The first is styled the Elder.
The Sukkah parallel places Rav after Huna in the report on the sacrifice. Heilprin’s proposed harmonization remains a gloss.
The corresponding Heilprin entry preserves the patronymic and the Yerushalmi transmission.
The precise expansion remains unselected. The Bavli, Rif and Rosh readings are directly known. Their evidence does not settle Heilprin’s siglum.
The gloss’s emendation remains attributed. Sukkah and Gittin differ in the final link and are preserved independently.
